```plato

    //==
    // # Catmull-Rom basis
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_Hermite_spline#Catmull-Rom_spline
    // Four control values; the segment runs from p1 (t=0) to p2 (t=1), with the
    // tangents taken from the neighbours p0 and p3 (uniform parameterization).
    //   CR(t) = 0.5 * [ 2*p1 + (p2 - p0)*t
    //                 + (2*p0 - 5*p1 + 4*p2 - p3)*t^2
    //                 + (3*p1 - p0 - 3*p2 + p3)*t^3 ]

    // The uniform Catmull-Rom segment at t, interpolating p1 to p2.
    CatmullRom(p0: INumerical, p1: INumerical, p2: INumerical, p3: INumerical, t: Number): INumerical
        => (p1 * 2.0
          + (p2 - p0) * t
          + (p0 * 2.0 + p2 * 4.0 - p1 * 5.0 - p3) * t.Square
          + (p1 * 3.0 + p3 - p0 - p2 * 3.0) * (t.Square * t)) * 0.5;

    // The first derivative (velocity) of the uniform Catmull-Rom segment:
    // 0.5 * [ (p2 - p0) + 2t*(2*p0 - 5*p1 + 4*p2 - p3) + 3t^2*(3*p1 - p0 - 3*p2 + p3) ].
    CatmullRomDerivative(p0: INumerical, p1: INumerical, p2: INumerical, p3: INumerical, t: Number): INumerical
        => ((p2 - p0)
          + (p0 * 2.0 + p2 * 4.0 - p1 * 5.0 - p3) * (2.0 * t)
          + (p1 * 3.0 + p3 - p0 - p2 * 3.0) * (3.0 * t.Square)) * 0.5;

    //==
    // # Evaluation of the declared polynomial types
    //
    // The array-backed forms fold their coefficient arrays with the P2 `Reduce`
    // primitive. Power-basis polynomials (dense, sparse, power series) evaluate
    // by Horner's rule below. The classical-basis series (Chebyshev, Legendre,
    // Hermite, Bernstein, Fourier) still await basis-specific recurrences
    // (Clenshaw / de Casteljau) rather than plain Horner; those are also
    // foldable but out of scope for this pass.

    // Evaluates a dense coefficient array given in ASCENDING powers at x by
    // Horner's rule (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horner%27s_method): folding
    // the highest-power coefficient first means no explicit power of x is ever
    // formed, which is both faster and more stable.
    // An empty array is the zero polynomial and evaluates to 0.
    HornerEval(coefficients: Array<Number>, x: Number): Number
        => MapRange(coefficients.Count, i => coefficients[coefficients.Count - 1 - i])
               .Reduce(0.0, (acc, c) => acc * x + c);

    // The value of the dense polynomial sum(Coefficients[k] * x^k) at x.
    Eval(p: Polynomial, x: Number): Number
        => HornerEval(p.Coefficients, x);

    // The value of the sparse polynomial sum(Coefficients[i] * x^Powers[i]) at
    // x. Each term forms its own power because the exponents are not contiguous.
    Eval(p: SparsePolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => MapRange(p.Powers.Count,
                    i => p.Coefficients[i] * x.Pow(p.Powers[i].ToNumber))
               .Reduce(0.0, (acc, term) => acc + term);

    // The value of the truncated power series sum(Coefficients[k]*(x-Center)^k)
    // at x, evaluated by Horner's rule in the shifted variable (x - Center).
    Eval(s: PowerSeries, x: Number): Number
        => HornerEval(s.Coefficients, x - s.Center);

    // The value of the single term Coefficient * x^Power at x.
    Eval(m: Monomial, x: Number): Number
        => m.Coefficient * x.Pow(m.Power.ToNumber);

    // The value of A*x^2 + B*x + C at x.
    Eval(p: QuadraticPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => p.A * x.Square + p.B * x + p.C;

    // The value of A*x^3 + B*x^2 + C*x + D at x.
    Eval(p: CubicPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => p.A * x.Square * x + p.B * x.Square + p.C * x + p.D;

    // The value of A*x^4 + B*x^3 + C*x^2 + D*x + E at x.
    Eval(p: QuarticPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => p.A * x.Square * x.Square + p.B * x.Square * x + p.C * x.Square + p.D * x + p.E;

    // The derivative of A*x^2 + B*x + C: 2*A*x + B.
    Derivative(p: QuadraticPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => 2.0 * p.A * x + p.B;

    // The derivative of A*x^3 + B*x^2 + C*x + D: 3*A*x^2 + 2*B*x + C.
    Derivative(p: CubicPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => 3.0 * p.A * x.Square + 2.0 * p.B * x + p.C;

    // The derivative of A*x^4 + ... + E: 4*A*x^3 + 3*B*x^2 + 2*C*x + D.
    Derivative(p: QuarticPolynomial, x: Number): Number
        => 4.0 * p.A * x.Square * x + 3.0 * p.B * x.Square + 2.0 * p.C * x + p.D;

    // The rational function's value at x: the Numerator's value over the
    // Denominator's, each by Horner's rule. Undefined at the Denominator's
    // roots (poles).
    Eval(r: RationalFunction, x: Number): Number
        => r.Numerator.Eval(x) / r.Denominator.Eval(x);
}
```
